items.title: Carolyn Buck Interview, 1969-03-25
items.q: Or Bobo. When Bobo came here. Lord, that child used to climb up on his bed all the time, hug him and kiss him and so forth.

ctx.x: Yes, I'd like you to say something about that, because that's one of the things I have nothing on. He didn't ever, none of the interviews I had with him, has ever matched his father as well.

Well, he was, when Bobo was taken from me, he knew that it worried me quite a bit. And he tried to reassure me that the boys usually, regardless of what happens, they'll never forget a mother, but there's just certain feelings that they have for a father. He says he remembers since he's been a child, that when his mother and father were separated, that he would go stay with his father for the weekend. And he's so proud, he said he'd be so proud walking down the street, sometimes he'd go downtown and get a shoe…
And he said, no, I'm not going to go into it.
